pluss::note::select¶

Back to Note Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Note pluss::note::select(series_range conditions, note_range choices,
                         const Note& default_value)
Note pluss::note::select(std::initializer_list<Series> conditions,
                         std::initializer_list<Note> choices,
                         const Note& default_value)
Note pluss::note::select(const Series& condition, const Note& choice,
                         const Note& default_value)
Note pluss::note::select(series_range conditions, note_range choices,
                         string_view default_value)
Note pluss::note::select(std::initializer_list<Series> conditions,
                         std::initializer_list<Note> choices,
                         string_view default_value)
Note pluss::note::select(const Series& condition, string_view choice,
                         string_view default_value)

The single-condition forms are one-branch shorthands. Any string_view choice or default is a scalar text cell — sugar for pluss::note::make(text).

Build A Note By Ordered Boolean Conditions¶

select() assembles one Note from a list of boolean Series conditions and a matching list of text choices. At every output cell it walks the conditions first to last and takes the choice paired with the first one that is true there; if none is true, default_value supplies the cell.

This is the text counterpart of pluss::series::select — an n-way, priority-ordered generalisation of “where”. It is the tool for turning several overlapping masks into a single labelled column: bucket names from numeric thresholds, status strings from a set of flags, a category per row from a cascade of predicates.

Ordering matters¶

Conditions are a priority list, not a set. Where two conditions are true at the same cell, the earlier one wins — later branches are fallbacks, not overrides. Put the most specific or highest-priority condition first.

Shapes and scalar broadcasting¶

An operand (condition, choice, or default) is scalar-like when it holds exactly one element; such an operand applies to every output cell. Every operand that is not scalar-like must have the same shape, and that shape is the output shape. So you can:

  • pair full-shaped conditions with full-shaped choices, or

  • pair full-shaped conditions with a single scalar choice that fills wherever that condition wins, or

  • give a scalar-like condition (a one-element true/false) that turns its whole branch on or off.

Requirements¶

  • At least one condition, and conditions.size() == choices.size().

  • Every condition must be a defined Bool-dtype Series. Numeric “truthiness” is not accepted — convert with a comparison first.

  • Every choice and the default must be defined.

  • The result is UTF-8 mode. All branches are read and shape-checked before assembly, so a malformed branch is an error even where its condition is false everywhere.

Example 1: Single Condition, Text Shorthand¶

const auto flags = pluss::make_series({true, false, true});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::select(flags, "YES", "no")) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["YES", "no", "YES"]

The scalar choice "YES" and default "no" broadcast across the condition’s three cells.

Example 2: Single Condition With Explicit Note Operands¶

const auto flags = pluss::make_series({true, false, true});
const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::select(
    flags, pluss::note::make("HIT"), pluss::note::make("miss"));
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["HIT", "miss", "HIT"]

Identical behavior to the shorthand — use this form when the choice is already a Note (for instance a full-shaped column).

Example 3: Two Ordered Conditions, First True Wins¶

const auto early = pluss::make_series({true, true, false, false});
const auto late  = pluss::make_series({false, true, true, false});

const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::select(
    {early, late},
    {pluss::note::make("early"), pluss::note::make("late")},
    "none");
pluss::note::print(std::cout, n) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["early", "early", "late", "none"]

At cell 1 both conditions are true and the earlier branch supplies "early". Cell 3 satisfies neither, so it takes the default.

Example 4: A Scalar Choice Broadcast Under A 2-D Condition¶

const auto mask = pluss::make_series({{true, false}, {false, true}});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::select(mask, pluss::note::make("X"), pluss::note::make("."))) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["X", "."], 
  [".", "X"]
]

The 2×2 condition sets the output shape; the scalar choice fills wherever the mask is true and the scalar default fills the rest.

Example 5: A Non-Boolean Condition Is Rejected¶

try {
  pluss::note::select(pluss::make_series({1, 0, 1}), "y", "n");
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg(e.what());
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

pluss::note::select: conditions must use Bool dtype

Pass a real boolean mask — series > 0, series == value, and so on.

Example 6: Condition And Choice Counts Must Match¶

const auto a = pluss::make_series({true});
try {
  pluss::note::select({a, a}, {pluss::note::make("x")}, "z");
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg(e.what());
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

pluss::note::select: condition/choice count mismatch
